reason: The test expects 'set session authorization u1@localhost' itself to fail with ER_MUST_CHANGE_PASSWORD (human fix: check in set_var_authorization::check). The agent instead lets the switch succeed but makes the new security context inherit the target user's password_expired state, so the password is no longer un-expired and the later SET PASSWORD / select 2 would behave as the test expects. The issue only shows that the expiry is lost, not whether SET AUTHORIZATION should be refused or keep the expiry, so the agent picked a different reasonable behaviour (weakness: switching to another user while expired is still allowed).

The agent relaxed DTCollation::aggregate globally for same-charset/same-derivation collations, which breaks existing behaviour: main.ctype_collate's 'CREATE TABLE t1 AS SELECT ' - ' AS a UNION SELECT getText()' no longer raises ER_CANT_AGGREGATE_NCOLLATIONS. The real root cause (the := assignment reporting DERIVATION_COERCIBLE instead of DERIVATION_USERVAR, checked by coercibility(@a:=...) = 5 in user_var) was not addressed.
EMPTY: the agent made no code change, so the mysqlbinlog --gtid-strict-mode default stays ON and the new mdev_29803 test still errors with out-of-order GTID.

The agent only inverted the interval comparison; with the copy path now taken for changed intervals, the full-struct Vers_part_info copy (which also copies now_part/hist_part pointers into the clone) breaks an existing test: 'alter table t1 partition by system_time interval 7 year' (MDEV-33370 case) now fails with ER_VERS_WRONG_PARTS. The human fix also stops copying now_part/hist_part and forces rebuild when alter_info->flags are set; the agent's patch regresses existing behaviour.

The agent only made the end-state check symmetric but kept json_skip_current_level, which after ']' consumes parent elements; results are wrong for several plain-semantics assertions: JSON_OVERLAPS('[[1],[2]]','[[],[2]]') returns 0 (expected 1, asymmetric with reverse), '[[[1],2]]' vs '[[[1],3]]' returns 1 (expected 0), and the object case returns 0 forward. These are correctness errors, not test-specific choices.

The server still crashes (signal 11 in String::append via Gis_polygon::simplify called from in_string::set) on the test's 'x' IN (..., ST_SIMPLIFY(...), ...) query. The agent fixed temporary String initialisation inside simplify but not the actual cause, the output buffer from the IN vector having a null charset (human fix: str->set_charset(&my_charset_bin) in Item_func_simplify::val_str).
